title: How a fast-delivery order is sourced, reserved and timed

hook.shape: One order's promise is pinned as a constant while a running clock starts, so every later step visibly spends from a fixed budget.

arc: Hook pins the promise and the clock → three viewer questions announced → one chapter per question, source then stock then speed → payoff on where the time goes.

beats.summary: A rider leaves a warehouse while a pinned promise and a running clock frame the whole trip, and a route draws from the store to the door.
Three questions the viewer would ask are listed up front and become the chapters that follow.
A route with a distance tag runs from a nearby warehouse to the customer, and the warehouse turns out to serve online orders only.
Each store's delivery area is drawn as a polygon, and a customer outside it gets no delivery at all.
With many overlapping areas, checking them one by one is shown as slow before any shortcut exists.
A grid drops over the map and only the customer's cell and the areas crossing it light up.
Payment succeeds and one unit is locked to the order, a second order for the same unit is rejected, and the stock count drops by one.
A time bar splits the promise between packing and riding, and a picker walks straight to a lit shelf slot because items sit in fixed places.

pacing: The pinned promise and running clock carry tension while the map underneath changes from beat to beat.
Each chapter question is asked and answered before the next appears, so the open sub-problem is always clear.
The concept beats stay short; most of the attention goes to the stock race and the split of the time budget.
